## Bottom line

Do not replace the current onboarding process with the automated proposal. It saves 100 staff minutes per case but produces 25 additional incorrect first submissions per 100 clients. That directly conflicts with the stated objective.

## Readiness — Infeasible as posed

Full automation is infeasible under the requirement not to sacrifice submission quality: reported correctness is 65%, versus 90% currently.

## Direction

Keep the current process as the production baseline. Treat automation only as a staff-assistance candidate—such as preparing drafts, pre-filling fields, or flagging issues—while staff retain final review.

Run a bounded pilot and adopt the hybrid only if it:

- Sustains at least the current 90% first-submission correctness.
- Produces a meaningful reduction from the two-hour baseline.
- Does not shift hidden work into corrections, client follow-up, or downstream processing.

Stop or redesign the pilot if correctness falls below 90%. Review after a representative sample rather than scaling from a few favourable cases. The evidence supports protecting quality now; it does not yet establish that a hybrid process will save time without degrading it.
